doc.title: Harry Edison — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

chapter: After Basie: freelancing, JATP and Hollywood
title: The Edison-Wess big band in Japan; LA big bands today
summary: The one-off Japan tour had many ex-Basie men; he also describes how tired he gets and how little he practices.

story.theme_name: Still working: current gigs, upcoming projects and plans
story.community_name: What's next: upcoming tours, records and plans

blocks.x: Was the closest you got the band that you and Frank Wess led not that long ago, was that over in Japan?
Yeah, Japan. We got the band together just for that engagement and after that when we got back to America, everybody went their own way.
But at least for that tour, you were able to….

It was a good band. It was a fantastic band and in fact, we had more Basie men in that band than was in the Frank Foster band. We had Al Grey, Snooky Young, and myself. Billy Mitchell, Eddie Jones, Marshall Royal.
Yeah, in fact, people had bought tickets for the Frank Foster concert and after…. End of CD #4
Sweets, you were just telling us about the tour to Japan with the band that you and Frank Wess co-led and had many Basie-ites in it.

As I was saying before, Frank Foster’s, the Basie band, they had already engaged in a tour of Japan and a lot of the people after they read the brochure of the Frank Wess band and myself, they went and exchanged their tickets to hear our band.

The Frank Foster band is not really a Basie alumni. Bill Hughes, Frank Foster, that’s the only one. But it was a good band, it was a really good band. We had a really good time over there and the album sounded terrific. But that’s the only engagement that we’ve had. And if we don’t get that again, we won’t have no more big band because there’s no place to play. Frank has one every now and then in New York, but I don’t participate in it because I couldn’t go from Los Angeles to New York just to play one or two gigs. If I lived around New York, naturally it would be a different situation.
And the big bands on the West Coast here in Los Angeles like the Juggernaut Band, Bill Berry’s band…

I go hear them but after a tour I feel like just laying on the couch. In fact, I put my horn here where I can look at it and I know I should practice because it’s laying right there but invariably I’ll pass by it and work the valves or something and hit one note. But that’s not enough practicing to do. You get so tired.
Well, according to what Basie told you, you hit that note and play the same damn note every night (both laugh)
Yeah, he was a good teacher
